project.name: cutover-entitlements
project.summary: a tenant entitlement service that migrated from a legacy policy engine to a new one, where the legacy engine's decisions and the new engine's decisions interact through an explicit cutover
project.whyProjectSpecific: the correct current standing depends on WHICH ENGINE evaluated a decision, WHEN the cutover happened, and WHICH TENANT CLASS the tenant belongs to. None of those is a software-engineering property, and none can be recovered from a maxim.

invariants.name: legacy-precedence-for-pre-cutover-decisions
invariants.historicalInitialRule: while the legacy engine was authoritative, a legacy DENY was final: no later ALLOW could overturn it, regardless of source.

revisions.rule: a legacy DENY is final for every tenant
revisions.reason: the legacy engine was the only authority

revisions.date: the new engine was introduced for NEW tenants
revisions.rule: for tenants onboarded AFTER the cutover, the new engine's ALLOW may overturn an inherited DENY
revisions.supersedes: revision 1, but ONLY for post-cutover tenants
revisions.reason: the new engine evaluates from its own policy set and an inherited legacy DENY is not part of its input

revisions.date: the cutover was made explicit and dated
revisions.rule: the tenant's OWN cutover date decides which precedence applies, not the date the tenant was created
revisions.reason: a tenant onboarded before the cutover may have been MIGRATED onto the new engine on a later date, and the migration date is what the contract now keys on

invariants.currentStanding: A legacy DENY outranks a newer inherited ALLOW ONLY for a tenant whose cutover date precedes the decision being evaluated. For a decision dated after that tenant's cutover date, the newer ALLOW wins, even though the DENY was recorded first.
invariants.applicability: applies to any decision where a DENY and an ALLOW both exist for the same tenant+capability and their recorded dates straddle the tenant's cutover date
limitations: it decides PRECEDENCE between two existing decisions; it does not create or delete either
it says nothing about two decisions on the SAME side of the cutover date, where ordinary latest-wins applies
the cutover date is per-tenant, so two tenants with identical decision histories can resolve differently
invariants.genericPriorCannotDetermine: a generic prior contains "deny usually wins" or "latest wins" but contains NO tenant cutover date, so it cannot decide which of the two applies to a given pair of decisions. The disambiguating fact is a date in this Project's history.
historicalArtifacts: the migration notes for the migrated tenant class
the incident where the precedence was applied wrongly
the revision that made the cutover date explicit

invariants.name: capability-alias-precedence-after-consolidation
invariants.historicalInitialRule: each capability had its own independent grant set, and a grant of one capability never affected another.

revisions.rule: three legacy capabilities were CONSOLIDATED into one new capability, and the legacy names became ALIASES of it
revisions.supersedes: revision 1 for the three consolidated capabilities only
revisions.reason: the new engine evaluates one capability, so the legacy names had to map onto it

revisions.rule: when a tenant holds a legacy alias and a grant of the consolidated capability, the CONSOLIDATED grant is authoritative and the alias grant is preserved but not counted twice
revisions.supersedes: the ambiguity about which of the two grants a revocation removes
revisions.reason: a revocation was removing the alias grant and leaving the consolidated one, so the tenant kept access the operator believed was removed

invariants.currentStanding: For the three consolidated capabilities, a legacy alias and the consolidated capability are the SAME authority. A revocation of either removes the tenant's access, and a tenant holding both does not hold two grants.
invariants.applicability: applies only to the three capabilities named in the consolidation record; every other legacy capability keeps its independent grant set
limitations: it does not rename or delete the legacy alias, which remains readable for historical queries
it does not apply to a legacy capability the consolidation record does not name
the consolidated grant is authoritative for COUNTING; the alias grant is preserved for provenance
invariants.genericPriorCannotDetermine: a generic prior contains "normalize aliases" but contains NO consolidation record, so it cannot know WHICH three legacy capabilities were consolidated, nor that the consolidated name is authoritative rather than the alias. The disambiguating facts are three capability names in this Project's history.
historicalArtifacts: the consolidation decision record naming the three capabilities
the revision that made the consolidated grant authoritative
the migration notes for alias holders

difficulty.sufficiencyLaw: the raw history must remain sufficient for a diligent worker to reconstruct the correct current standing
difficulty.forbiddenPreTestClaim: do not claim that the model lacks the knowledge empirically before testing

diagnosticClasses.statement: a legacy DENY recorded BEFORE the tenant cutover is final against a later ALLOW
from the tenant cutover onward the newer ALLOW wins, even though the DENY was recorded first
an ALLOW recorded before the cutover is NOT protected, so a later DENY wins
two tenants with identical decision histories resolve differently when their cutover dates differ
revoking an alias the tenant holds removes access even when the tenant also holds the consolidated name
revoking an alias the tenant does NOT hold removes nothing
a capability outside the consolidation keeps an independent grant set
a resolution before the earliest decision sees nothing

H.name: RAW_HISTORY
H.receives: current Project world, the declared raw Project history corpus, and ordinary worker tools
H.selectedCapital: EMPTY — canonical capital assets and associations exist, but the selected set is empty

C.name: CAPITALIZED
C.receives: exactly the same world and raw-history corpus, plus the frozen current-standing selected capital handles through the governed Context/pull mechanism
C.selectedCapital: the frozen current-standing set, selected through the governed mechanism

armOrderBalance.law: the frozen randomization must place each arm first in at least one block, or arm order is confounded with block order

retryPolicy.rule: a valid generation outcome is NEVER retried; an infrastructure-invalid generation is retried only to reach the scheduled session count
retryPolicy.infrastructureInvalidDefinition: the child failed to run, the worker failed to spawn, or the host lost the job — NOT a bad model outcome

POSITIVE_SIGNAL.requirement: C reads fewer raw-history bytes than H in at least 3 of 4 matched blocks; C reads fewer raw-history artifacts than H in at least 3 of 4 blocks; C terminal invariant quality is not worse than H in at least 3 of 4 blocks; every C trajectory demonstrates governed capital consumption; no C trajectory suffers an excess completion-budget failure relative to its matched H solely hidden by averaging

ADVERSE_SIGNAL.requirement: C has consistently greater reconstruction/search cost or worse invariant/completion outcomes in at least 3 of 4 blocks

compressionVerdictRules.pValues: NOT REPORTED — §19 forbids p-values at n=4

netCostVerdictRules.law: the net-cost verdict is reported separately and must not silently overwrite the reconstruction-compression verdict

correctnessInterpretation.textbookEffect: if H and C both reach full final correctness but C requires substantially less historical reconstruction, that is a valid positive result
